title: fix(cloud-connection): a cloud-fetched marketplace install of a package shipping a catalog name an environment-authored item holds writes its ledger entry, and the next cold boot refuses; refuse it before the first write
body:
Filing gate **③**: a finding of the contract review of PR #25355 (#24446 U2; record 6356845701, escalation E2). It is pre-existing and outside that PR's surface.
- **Who acts:** the shared queue.
- **Dedupe:** none.

Part of #24446. That card's U1 GO (6353222762) named the pre-write collision check as U2's. This card carries it instead, because the defect is in the install door's registration, not in the access comparison.

## What is on `main` (as read at PR #25355's head `ac8ce968`)
- **The rule:** a package may not ship a security catalog name (position, permission set, capability) that an environment-authored item already holds. Registration refuses the second holder (`objectql` `registry.ts` near `:3081` and `:5960`), and a boot that finds such a pair refuses (`refuseEnvironmentHeldSecurityCatalogNames`, `objectql/src/plugin.ts` near `:2517`; ruling A on #22307).
- **The inline-manifest branch** of `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` meets that refusal before its first write: 422.
- **The cloud-fetched branch registers leniently.** It writes the ledger entry, and the install answers success. **The next cold boot then refuses**, so a deployment that took that upgrade cannot restart until an operator removes one of the two holders.
- **How it is reached:** a customer clones a vendor permission set or position under a name, and a later version of that vendor's package ships the same name.
- **Not caught by U2:** U2's access check projects the incoming manifest over the registry. The projection's catalog `list` drops a same-name entry of another holder, so the clone is replaced in the projection instead of being reported.

## Wanted
- **Measure first.** Confirm both branches on the current `main`. Name every install door that can register such a name:
  - the marketplace door, both branches;
  - `POST /api/v1/packages` with `overwrite` (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`);
  - any other door.
- **Fix:** every door refuses before its first write when the incoming package ships a catalog name an environment-authored item holds. The refusal is an ADR-0112 code naming each colliding name and its holder, like the inline branch. Prefer one shared pre-write check over a copy per door.
- This is a refusal, not a confirmable finding. A confirmed install would still leave a boot that refuses.

## Acceptance
- On each door and each catalog type, an incoming name held by an environment-authored item is refused before any write, with nothing registered and no ledger entry. It is pinned with a CONTROL: no collision installs unchanged.
- A deployment that has taken such an upgrade on today's `main` gets an operator remedy, stated in the changeset.
- R1–R4 hold, with R4 measured under `isolated` and `group`.
